## Reporting rule for every answer

Report every proportion as a percentage rounded to **one decimal place**, and
name the reference group in words. Write "40.0% of commuters", not "0.4",

# STAT 110 (synthetic) — Lecture notes

## §1 Conditional probability

§1.1 P(A | B) is read "the probability of A among B". It answers: of the
cases in group B, what share are also in A?

§1.2 Compute it as (number of cases in both A and B) divided by (number of
cases in B). The denominator is the reference group B, not the whole sample.

§1.3 The order matters. P(A | B) and P(B | A) usually differ because they use
different reference groups. Before computing, decide which group the question
restricts you to; that group is the denominator.

§1.4 Assume every case is equally weighted and the reference group is not
empty.

## §2 Two-way tables

§2.1 A two-way table counts cases by two categorical variables at once, one in
the rows and one in the columns, with row totals and column totals.

§2.2 A row percentage divides a cell by its row total; a column percentage
divides a cell by its column total. Choosing row versus column percentages is
the same decision as choosing the reference group in §1.2.

§2.3 Row percentages in one row add to 100%; column percentages in one column
add to 100%. Percentages across a row of column percentages need not.

## §3 Grouped summaries

§3.1 A grouped summary splits the cases by a categorical variable and computes
one summary value (such as a mean or a count) per group.

§3.2 The result has one row per non-empty group, not one row per original case.

§3.3 Compare groups using the same summary; do not compare a group mean with a
group total.
# STAT 110 (synthetic) — Practice set A (T1 conditional probability)

Answer keys are in practice-key.md. Use the outline's reporting rule.

**Q1.** A class has 40 students. 25 of them commute. 10 of the commuters cycle
to campus. What percentage of commuters cycle?

**Q2.** A company has 60 employees. 24 of them work remotely. 6 of the remote
workers are trainees. What percentage of remote workers are trainees?

**Q3.** A club has 30 members. 12 of them are seniors. 4 of the seniors
volunteer at events. What percentage of seniors volunteer?

**Q4.** A store had 45 shoppers today. 20 of them ordered online. 9 of the
online shoppers returned an item. What percentage of online shoppers returned
an item?

# STAT 110 (synthetic) — Midterm 1, 2025 (past paper)

**1.** Of 50 surveyed drivers, 30 own an electric car, and 12 of the electric
car owners charge at work. What percentage of electric car owners charge at
work?

**2.** Write the null and alternative hypotheses for testing whether the mean
commute time differs from 30 minutes, and state what a p-value of 0.03 means
at the 5% level.

**3.** A grouped summary computes the mean score for each of 4 sections of a
course with 120 students. How many rows does the result have?
